title: Pneumatic control valve sticking, wet instrument air
tests: Cross-asset link to compressor and dryer; instrument faults repeatedly replaced.
summary: A level control valve on a thickener feed sticks and hunts; the positioner has been replaced twice. Moisture and oil are in the instrument air. The air dryer has been in alarm for weeks. The tree stops at 'positioner faulty'.

problem.title: Level control valve LV-3306 sticking, positioner replaced twice
problem.site: Nickel concentrator, thickener area, Kalgoorlie WA
problem.whatHappened: LV-3306 started sticking and hunting on 18 Sep 2026, causing tank level swings and an overflow to the bund. The positioner was replaced on 18 Sep and again on 2 Oct; the valve stuck again on 9 Oct. Water and oil were found in the positioner air filter.
problem.where: Positioner and actuator air supply on LV-3306.
problem.when: Worst in the early morning; air dryer high dew point alarm active for 3 weeks.
problem.impact: Thickener level swings, one overflow to the bund, operators on manual for several shifts.
problem.makeModel: 150 mm globe control valve, pneumatic diaphragm actuator with smart positioner
problem.duty: Controls feed to a thickener, continuous

evidence.title: Positioner air filter
evidence.note: Water and oil emulsion in the filter bowl. Rust spots on the regulator.

evidence.title: Instrument air dew point trend
evidence.note: Dew point above alarm limit for 3 weeks; dryer drain not releasing.

evidence.title: Work orders for LV-3306
evidence.note: Two positioner replacements and one air filter clean in 3 weeks. No WO on the dryer alarm.

evidence.title: Actuator diaphragm and stem
evidence.note: Stem sticking from corrosion on the guide; diaphragm intact.

mustSuggest.idea: Wet and oily instrument air contaminating the positioner and corroding the stem guide
Instrument air dryer failing (drain not releasing, dew point alarm)
Dryer alarm raised no work order, so a known problem had no owner
Instrument air dew point not on the maintenance monitoring or round

acceptable: Air filter regulator not draining automatically
wrongOrDangerous: Replace with a different positioner brand as the answer

mustFlag.note: Restates the symptom; two replacements did not fix it

mustNotFlag: stopped_at_physical without noting that the real cause lies on another asset
challenge.expectation: Questions: what did the air filter show; what is upstream; why did the dryer alarm not generate a job?
deliberateWeaknesses: n1 verified, no evidence; positioner replacement twice shows it was not the cause
Root n2 is a restatement of the symptom (weak_logic)
e1 to e4 are not used
No link to the instrument air dryer, a separate asset
No human or system cause: alarm on the dryer for 3 weeks with no WO

capa.deteriorationReasoning: Moisture and oil in the air corroded the stem guide and fouled the positioner. That is contamination we allowed, not wear.
corrective: Dryer repair and instrument air blow-down, replace the filter regulator and clean or replace the stem guide

preventive.what: Service the instrument air dryer and check the drain
preventive.interval: every 3 months, starting point to check with the dryer maker

preventive.what: Instrument air dew point read on rounds or on the DCS with an alarm and a work order raised from the alarm
Alarm response procedure so a dryer alarm raises a priority job
Filter regulator with auto drain on each control valve air supply, if a review supports it
Hold a spare positioner and filter regulator for this valve type

capa.spares: Positioner and filter regulator for this valve family; replacement had a 14 day lead time.
capa.rollout: Other valves and instruments on the same air header: check filters for water and oil, and inspect stems.
unacceptable: Invented dew point limits presented as a standard
